This study presents a dynamic equivalent of the POISSON HOREWAVUE transform, named the Time-Dependent POISSON HOREWAVE transform. Utilizing this new tool, a time-varying POISSON AUTOREGressive model, called the POISSON TAREWAVE model, is developed. A comparison between the POISSON HWAVE and the existing POISSON filter reveals that the former retains more information. Furthermore, the paper examines the performance of the POISSON TAREWAVE model using simulated and real-world data, demonstrating its ability to effectively predict future outcomes and identify underlying factors that contribute to them.

tests: we've developed and validated an approach that links optical photometry data from short-exposure images to output from long-exposure images to create a precise method for determining air quality from images of the night sky. Results: our team achieved an accuracy of 3 parts per million in measuring CDE based on laboratory tests, validating the method's effectiveness. Benefits: this technique can greatly expand the scope of existing weather monitors like ALL-SkY NET to monitor global aerosol conditions at no cost, benefiting the system and enabling new research possibilities.

Our research presents an efficient configurational molecular sampling method through Langevin dynamics, achieved with an iterative solver that obviates explicit inversion of the Hessian matrix.  Our iterative approach approximates the force on each particle as harmonic around its previous position, allowing for an implicit time integration step that's first-order in the time step $\tau$ and also exhibits first-order accuracy in energy calculation.  Given these properties, we believe our method is suitable for configurational molecular sampling.  We validated our algorithm's effectiveness and efficiency through several classic test cases, including Lennard-Jones and Krypton systems, as well as a biomolecular example, showing that it outperforms existing methods, especially in systems with dense local minima.  In contrast to alternative approaches that are first-order in $\tau$ but require second-order methods like Molecular Dynamics for sampling, our second-order Langevin dynamics algorithm offers unique benefits.

A growing number of image description evaluation metrics have incorporated human-generated benchmark datasets, leading to the emergence of correlation-based evaluation methods. Recently, there has been an surge in the production of large-scale human datasets for specific visual tasks, prompting the consideration of utilizing them for evaluating artificial intelligence generators. However, we identify and discuss several issues with this approach through a systematic examination of visual tasks and their descriptions. Firstly, we find that human descriptions often contain subjective elements that do not accurately represent the outcomes of specific visual tasks. Secondly, we discover that large-scale human datasets typically consist of descriptions generated by a diverse group of individuals for varied purposes, which may not be representative for evaluation objectives. To address these issues, we propose a platform that enables researchers to conduct specific visual tasks and evaluate corresponding description generators in a manner that is tailored to their individual needs. As demonstration, we generated a new description evaluation dataset and conducted targeted experiments to validate our suggestions.

We provide a novel and dynamic method to calculate the rational conformal field theory intricacy functional $I(\tf)$ for functional CFT models within an associated vector model framework. By leveraging the intricate functional model and the vector model re-formulation, we're able to determine the polynomial invariants of multiple variables $\I(\\v\)) for an intricate system of differential equations known as the Arnold-Euler equation flow. These equations define a broader class of spacetime dynamics for restricted CFT models.

Based on an extension of the lambda CDM model called the baryon oscillation spectral model, our research team uses the O'Mera solver to predict the properties of rare baryons and mesons that occur through oscillating quantum fluctuations.

This article presents variations of a novel waveforming technique described in our prior work on integrated energy and data transmission. The primary approach, MISO-OFDM-MD, utilizes multiple antennas and frequency channels to enhance data rates, building on a base system that transmits information and energy through a single antenna and frequency channel, SISO-OFDM-MD. Both the SISO-OFDM-MD and SISO-OFDM/MD systems, along with their extended versions SISO-OFDM-MD and OFDM systems, have been evaluated through simulations to assess their performance in terms of achieving desired data rates and power requirements while maximizing outcomes.

We present a framework for statistically rigorous particle data PDF fitting, addressing the challenge that standard Monte Carlo methods like EM and Expectation-decomposition do not directly apply due to the probabilistic nature of likelihood evaluation. Our Expectation-Score method fills this gap, enabling PDF fitting operations that account for measurement correlations and normalize cross-section functions at all x and Q^2 points with robust statistical grounding.

This study uses an advanced, linearized modeling approach to investigate the interaction between flame turbulence and acoustic waves in a methane-air jet flame in a co-flowing environment. To begin, a baseline model of the jet flame is created. Then, to better predict the flame's behavior in an acoustic environment, the model is linearized by considering the jet flame as an active flame. To simulate the turbulent environment, instantaneous velocity fields are superimposed on the model. To mimic the interaction with acoustic waves, Kelvin-Helmholtz instability is utilized. The resulting models, which take into account velocity fluctuations, are used to predict the flame's shape and temperature distribution. To evaluate the models' accuracy, the predicted flame shape and temperature distribution are compared to high-speed schlieren images and spectroscopic measurements. The results show that the models accurately reproduce the flame shape and that the imposed disturbances cause the flame to wrinkle. Notably, the models also predict the emergence of a standing wave pattern in response to acoustic forcing, which is confirmed by the experimental data. The active flame approach is found to be particularly effective in simulating the interaction between the jet flame and acoustic waves, and the models are found to be effective in predicting the resulting flame shape and temperature distribution under the influence of acoustic waves.

This article examines Mordachev, Muzinich and Weinberg's nonlocal gravity theory, focusing on its background framework and connection to materiality. The fundamental frame in this theory consists of three fields: a scalar, vector, and tensor field. We explain how these fields function within the theory and discuss their potential relevance to cosmology. Additionally, we outline the constitutive relations required to connect the framework to cosmological models, with suggestions on how these models might be refined for better integration with nonlocal gravity theory.

This paper provides an in-depth summary of small-scale particle interactions to be investigated with current and upcoming accelerators on the LHC and its upgraded 100 GeV superconducting ion liner (SOLIS) ion liner, focusing on exotic particles that are weakly interacting such as axions and other similar particles, as well as other understudied multi-particle systems consisting of charged and neutral hadrons. A variety of possible new physics scenarios that can be investigated through these minor systems is discussed, including searches for weakly interacting exotic particles, as well as investigations into heavy exotic particles and their potential applications in future accelerators with higher energies. In addition, possible strategies for detecting these systems and relevant data requirements are explored in detail, along with possible theoretical and experimental research directions that could be undertaken.

Recent observations by the VLT show that the mass of the star I2018a around the Galactic Centre is actually that of a neutron star, expanding the group of stellar mass binaries in the central 100 parsecs of the Milky Way from four to five members. This discovery raises two main questions: what causes these binary systems containing a neutron star to become X-ray emitting, and what leads to their recurrence? To address these issues, we have developed a recurrence model that takes into account the different mechanisms of mass transfer in these binaries. In this model, the neutron star in the system can form an accretion disk through tidal torques if it's in a wide binary configuration with the companion star, similar to what is seen in systems like HerX and RXJ1550-5746. However, in closer binary configurations, direct transfer of matter from the companion star to the neutron star through Roche lobe overflow can also occur, as observed in systems like 4U1725-304 and4U1636-536. By comparing the recurrence intervals of these known binaries with those of other X-ray binaries in the Milky Way, we find that the model accurately predicts the recurrence intervals of these systems when different parameters such as the initial semi-major axis and mass ratio are varied, as long as the total mass of the binary system remains consistent.

Bipartite graphs represent connections between two distinct groups of objects, and their visualization often involves laying out the groups in parallel lines with edges drawn horizontally. A special variation of this visualization is considered polynomial time to create, but achieving a specific edge crossing pattern known as a bi-circular layout is NP-hard. The challenge of circularizing the bi-circular layout is shown to be fixed-parameter tractable with respect to the number of edge crossings. After creating this layout, the number of crossings can be effectively removed if the number of connections within each group is limited.

This study presents a novel side-channel attack, HyperDegrade, designed to exploit the information leakage caused by power leakage during aggressive GPU frequency downgrading. By leveraging the relationship between leakage magnitude and degradation speed, we developed an efficient algorithm to decode cached data. Our experiments demonstrated that HyperDegrade can compromise a target buffer in approximately 10 seconds, achieving an attack success rate of over 99%. Furthermore, we found that HyperDegrade's effectiveness is influenced by the initial leakage and the efficiency of the underlying frequency-downgrading technique. To mitigate these factors, we developed an optimized aggressive frequency-downgrading method, HyperAccelerate, which leverages context to enhance leakage and decrease its variability. Our results showed that HyperAccelerate can improve HyperDegrade's efficiency by up to two orders of magnitude. We believe that our findings provide valuable insights into leveraging leakage that arises from aggressive voltage and frequency scaling side-channels.

The Discrepancy Analysis (DA) theory, a specialized form of knot theory, is noted for its applicability beyond knot theory, including its use in studying links with disjoint and intersecting crossings. The paper discuses the Disentangling Operation (EO) that the DA theory can incorporate to Disjoint and Intersecting links with Discrepancy Analysis (DEIA). The EO operation is described as a three-move process that can separate even the most intricate links formed by disjoint and intersecting lines. The first move involves a basic displacement, the second involves a twist or unwinding of intersecting lines, and the final move involves translating one line around another. This operation is shown to be equivalent to the DEIA analysis and can be used to completely disentangle any linked structure. The new Disentangling Equivalence Theorem is described as a combination of the DEIA and EO operations that can completely separate any linked form that the DA theory is applicable to.

This paper explores how a group of networked robots can coordinate their activities on multiple tasks to maximize total performance. We develop a theory to determine the best coordination strategy to achieve this goal. Using a recursive approach, we derive optimal solutions for all situations a group of robots might encounter. We also present a strategic game to illustrate our findings and confirm their validity through simulations.

This study aims to establish the permutation group theory framework, highlighting key concepts such as group actions, the size of the framework, and the distinction between regular and semi-regular frameworks. Key framework includes the construction of the framework graph, the framework matrix, and the framework tree, as well as the framework of infinite sets. we discuss the framework of subgroups, including the framework of abelian, solvable, and cyclic subgroups, as well as the framework of affine and linear groups. the Jordan's and Schreier-Ulam-Tits theorems on framework of abelian and solvable subgroups are discussed. The framework of wreath products and the framework of infinite sets are also described.

The detection capabilities of advanced gravitational wave detectors are hindered in the high-frequency range by the quantum limitations of measurement and signal loss within interferometer systems. innovative designs in interferometer topologies are being explored to mitigate these signal losses. This paper evaluates the potential benefits of a novel configuration called the sloshing Sagnac interferometer, which features a non-linear topology, on the sensitivity limitations of gravitational wave detectors. Numerical analyses indicate that this design could lead to improved high-frequency sensitivity for these detectors. Furthermore, an optimal signal recycling gain is identified for the sloshing Sagnac interferometer when utilized with the LIGO detector, and the gains in sensitivity are being analyzed in the context of gravitational wave detection capabilities.

Recent large-scale MIMO systems are considered an exciting development, but their potential benefits are limited by hardware constraints and complex processing requirements. To address these issues, new protocols are being developed that utilize intersection-free visibility regions for data transmission between the system and users. This research proposal aims to use these intersection-free regions in a random access protocol for the system and users. The protocol involves the L-MIMO system sharing visible regions with users, who then report non-intersecting parts of the regions to help the system transmit data in a way that avoids interference. An optimal rule for selecting users for transmission is derived to maximize the protocol's throughput, taking into account the dynamic nature of passive radio frequency identification scanning. Additionally, the best region for the system to scan is identified to further enhance performance. Through simulation, the proposed protocol is shown to outperform existing methods in throughput, and region identification is found to contribute significantly to the protocol's success.

This study explores neural text generation techniques by building on an $N$-gram language model through residual learning and fine-tuning. The proposed framework, which incorporates the $N$-gram base with a neural residual module, has been found to significantly outperform both traditional neural and $n$-gram models through extensive evaluations on large-scale datasets from Wikipedia and Wikititles. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach leads to substantial improvements in language modeling performance, especially when assessed through automatic and human satisfaction measures. Furthermore, the findings confirm the scalability of the proposed method, which can process vast datasets containing billions of tokens and millions of unique $n$-grams with efficient memory usage and training times. The results also highlight the benefits of combining deep neural networks with classical language models, which share a common objective of language modeling, and the potential for further research into hybrid approaches.

This investigation in inverted documents processing began with the neural network-based approaches around 2014, quickly seeing a surge in performance until late 2017 and initially with global average accuracy rates of around 85% in October 2019. The most recent results presented in Giga- and Ultra-Neural models in May 2019 showed promising outcomes with results around 91-99%. However, political document analysis often involves challenging characteristics such as unusual layouts, low contrast, and distorted pages that often cause neural-based approaches to fall short. On average, these models struggle with accuracy rates of around 80%, with errors often stemming from misrecognised characters and skipped pages. On contrasted attempts, neural models often misrecognise blurred text and are outperformed by established techniques. The need was identified for an informed optical character recognition approach that leverages ballot tally machine features and prior knowledge to enhance the accuracy of political document analysis. The proposed model, which employed a combination of pre-process steps, tailorable architectures, and a training set derived from pre-existing tools and sample scanned pages, showed improved outcomes. The results demonstrated pre-existing accuracy rates of around 99.9%, pre-existing speed rates of around 90%, and pre-existing memory efficiency rates of 10% or less were exceeded. The need was identified for further research on the selection of the pre-processing model, the use of unsupervised clustering techniques,

This and following research focuses on investigating and documenting various atmospheric circulation patterns in computer-simulated models of Earth-like atmospheres with complex thermal dynamics. Using 3D thermal dynamics simulations in a Enclosing model that accurately depicts our planet's rotation and thermal conditions, researchers observed and analyzed various circulation patterns that develop in the thermally simulated atmosphere. As the model decreases the thermal contrast between the equator and the poles, three primary circulation patterns emerge: a five-cell circulation system with multiple jets near the equator, a single-cell pattern with the Coriolis effect influencing movement near the poles, and a single-cell pattern with a super-rotation pattern centered around the equator. Additionally, as the thermal differential increases, a circulation model that aligns with Earth's five-cell pattern is observed in moderate thermal conditions, a single-cell pattern without jet formation is seen in mild thermal conditions, and a five-cell circulation pattern with a five-cell circulation system is noticed in extreme thermal conditions.
This study formulates two integral integral expressions to represent the reciprocal Gamma function, validating their validity through numerical evaluation.

This study develops a sophisticated mathematical model, specifically a nonlinear integral equation Desay-Schofield equation within a phase-space framework for bosonic systems to investigate the dynamics of a two-dimensional Bose gas in equilibrium. By leveraging an instantaneous random quantum hydrodynamic method proposed by the authors and employing a numerical simulator, a variety of physical properties such as velocity auto-correlation functions and collective excitation patterns were analyzed. Notably, the results obtained from the simulator align with the QSay-Schofield equation's predictions, and a slight discrepancy with Mean Field theory was observed. Furthermore, a phase-space Wigner function was employed to examine the system's Weyl symbols and observe their time evolution.

The surge in available knowledge has made it increasingly important to effectively organize and extract information from vast knowledge bases within the AI community. Incremental knowledge learning (IKL) and multi-domain knowledge learning (MKL) technologies are pivotal in automating the organization and adaptation of pre-trained models. The Instructor-Student collaborative framework, consisting of a Knowledge Processor and a Knowledge Updater, has gained significant traction due to its efficiency and effectiveness. The Knowledge Processor integrates various strategies like hashing, projection, and knowledge graphs to organize knowledge, while the Knowledge Updater utilizes techniques such as parameter sharing, adaptation, and continuation to update models. A comprehensive review of the Instructor-Student collaborative framework is provided, covering its application in IKL and multi-domain knowledge learning, analysis of its performance and theoretical underpinnings, and an overview of real-world implementations and future research directions. The framework's versatility is highlighted through its application in various domains, and the need for more large-scale, diverse knowledge sources and in-depth performance analyses is emphasized. The Instructor-Student collaborative framework is anticipated to contribute significantly to the development of personalized and adaptive AI systems in knowledge erosion environments.

We introduce a new efficient method for representing functions within graphical models, particularly for use in constrained optimization tasks such as finding the maximum probability explanation (MPE). Our approach deviates from traditional table-based representations, which often lead to a state space explosion during the variable elimination process employed by exact optimization algorithms. Instead, we utilize simple mathematical functions to represent scaled potentials, significantly reducing memory usage and enhancing the efficiency of the Viterbi algorithm when dealing with linear chains. Our experiments using TIMIT and ATIS speech recognition datasets demonstrate that, when applied to the linear chain graphical model, our proposed approach yields more accurate results with far less memory usage compared to the standard table-based method.

Recently introduced is a higher rank algebra known as the Racah algebra $R(n)$, which serves as a special case of the centralizer $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2$. This centralizer can be represented as a quotient of a commutative algebra $R_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, which is generated by the variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$ over $\mathfrak{sl}_2$. We define a sequence of ideals within $R_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, denoted as $I_m(n)$, where $R_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)/I_m(n)$ is equivalent to the truncated algebra $R_m(n)$ for $m \leq n$ and the Racah algebra for $n < m$. This allows us to define a graded version of the racah algebra, called the Hilbert-Poincare series of $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$, denoted as $H_p(Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)))$. For the case of $n=4$, we demonstrate that this series can be factored into two Jacobi theta functions, which in turn can be related to the algebra $A_5^{(1)}(2)$, also known as the exceptional Lie algebra $E_8$, at its minusc

The paired permutation test is frequently used to identify discrepancies between pairs of systems, such as in software evaluation, with paired permutation testing being a more in-depth version of the process. A key component of this testing process is accurately shuffling data, which can be challenging when dealing with large systems that have numerous performance metrics. In such cases, certain combination rules used to determine test statistics may produce inconsistent values after permutation, potentially leading to unreliable results. To address this challenge, a new algorithm called paired-paired permutation testing has been developed, which utilizes a theoretical graph to determine a valid reordering method that preserves the integrity of test statistics. This algorithm, which is found to be efficient and effective through both simulated and real-world experiments, ensures more reliable when comparing two systems directly.

Our research group has utilized the theoretical framework of the multiphase transport model to investigate the influence of initial anisotropy and pressure gradient on triangular flow $v_3$ in both Cu+Cu and Au+Au collisions, with a focus on mid-central and mid-peripheral interactions at an energy level of 200 GeV. Through the analysis of Cu+Cu collisions, it was found that a initial anisotropy in a triangular pattern leads to a greater triangular flow $v_3$ compared to a lateral displacement in a square pattern. Similarly, when examining Au+Au collisions, the results demonstrated that a initial anisotropy in a triangular pattern results in a higher triangular flow $v_3$ compared to a initial anisotropy in a square pattern. Furthermore, the model's predictions aligned well with experimental data for both Cu+Cu and Au+Au collisions. Based on the results obtained, it was found that triangular flow $v_3$ is influenced by initial geometric configurations in a manner that is analogous to elliptical flow $v_2$ in central heavy-ion collisions. Consequently, triangular flow $v_3$ can be utilized as a tool to probe the quark-gluon plasma viscosity in heavy-ion collisions.

This study presents a refined version of the Poisson multi-Bernoulli (PMB) filter, focusing on how sensors are managed, with the assumption that new targets appear on a grid system. A key modification introduces a more general grid cell as the prediction step for the density component, utilizing a grid-based particle filter to estimate the density within each grid cell. A specific management scheme is proposed where a single sensor is directed to a non-information-grained grid cell chosen at random from all possible cells. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach.

The dynamics of soccer games include moments of heightened intensity where a team with a pending goal requires precise and swift decision-making capabilities. In these scenarios, we are investigating whether a robot teammate can provide valuable goal predictions to aid players in making quick decisions. In a fast-paced soccer game, making decisions is often done through brief gestures or signals, which limits the range of actions that can be taken. To address this constraint, we are proposing a game framework that incorporates goal prediction actions, along with existing movement and passing options. Additionally, we are introducing a realistic soccer game simulator that provides goal prediction training data, as well as an incentive system that values goal scoring highly. Through experiments conducted on a dataset from a professional soccer league, we have found that deep reinforcement learning can effectively incorporate goal prediction actions into the game's incentive structure, resulting in winning large majority of games when started from goal-scoring situations.

The advancement of high-speed computing and optics technology has enabled LDV systems to obtain two-dimensional deformation maps of large areas with single-point sensors, which is significant for industries such as aerospace where large-area monitoring is critical. However, when using a single LDV system to measure large areas, the issue of coherence loss due to the expansion of the measurement area remains a challenge. To address this issue, we proposed a method to obtain 2D deformation maps of a large area with a single LDV system by incorporating an encoder to track the changes in the optical path length of the probe beam and developing a real-time post-processing algorithm to correct the recorded data, which is novel as it restores the system's coherence loss without requiring additional hardware. Experiments showing the effectiveness of the technique with both sinusoidal and impact loading demonstrate the method's ability to accurately capture the true deformation of a sample even under large-amplitude loading conditions, which is important for engineering applications where high dynamic range is critical.

This paper provides precise definitions of spectral and orbital stability for a system of interacting particles, anharmonic oscillator and Klein-Gordon equation. It also clarifies the conditions required to prove either type of stability. Using this definition, it's shown that the linearized equation of the system has no unstable spectral components lying on the imaginary axis outside of the set of linearized equation's natural frequencies. Additionally, it establishes that both the anharmonic oscillator and the Klein-Gordon equation exhibit orbital stability when their frequencies match.

In experiments involving particle collisions, observables that deviate from predictions indicate new physics. While deviations in $D$ decays have already been explained by non-$CP$-violating effects, anomalies in $B$ decays require a presence of new physics. To investigate this, we develop a framework for estimating the effectiveness of an alien pseudoscalar at the Belle II experiment, taking into account $B$ decay mechanisms including angular momentum violation and $CP$-violation, both usual and rare. Using recent data from Belle I, we derive limits on the coupling strength between an PSP and photons for various $B$ decay modes. Although existing limits from $B\bar{B}$ event samples and $CP$-violating measurements are noted, generally weaker limits on the coupling are found when considering specific decay modes. To enhance detection capabilities, we propose searching for $D\bar{D}$ and $K\bar{K}_S$ decays as well as additional sources of rare and $CP$-violating $B$ decays at the Belle II experiment.

Recent advances in contextualized language modeling have shown promising results on semantic change detection through scores like GLUE and SOTA, but these outcomes may be artificially inflated due to optimal performance on word and phrase analogy tasks. This study reveals that contextualized models tend to confuse grammar and semantics, leading to similar performance drops after applying alteration operators such as negation and questioning. Building on these findings, researchers develop a multi-stage semantic change detection model that outpervents state-of-the-art scores, by initially employing a discrete transformation to convert semantic alterations into explicit modifications before analysis.

Active galactic nuclei, including the simplest and most complex entities, can potentially be used to narrow down the mass range of ultralight bosons through a phenomenon called superradiance, forming an energy ladder of allowed masses. In this research, we analyze the spin characteristics of heavy entities, such as gamma-ray blazars and X-ray binary AGN, to determine the effective mass range of ultralight bosons through spin measurement, providing an alternative method to determine allowable mass ranges without requiring a knowledge of entity mass, filling a deficiency in existing research, and enabling a more precise mapping of allowed mass ranges through a combination of previous findings and our new discoveries, resulting in Percent-Collected Coverage of 68% at frequency resolutions of 10^-2, 10^-1, and 10^0 Hz, and Percent-Directed Exclusion of 71%, 25%, and 3% at frequency resolutions of 10^-2, 10^-1, and 10^0 Hz, within the range of 10^-3 to 10^3 Hz, per an assumption of self-decay times of 10^5 years, self-decay times of 10^7 years, self-decay times of 10^8 years, and self-decay times of 10^9 years, respectively, comparing favorably with previous results and demonstrating the

A complex task in theoretical physics involves analyzing a quantum harmonic harmonic oscillator under a linear driving force under a complex scenario under complex situation.  The paper describes the process of obtaining the steady-state of the system by employing a path integral approach and a Metropolis-Hastings algorithm.  The complex scenario under discussion involves the computation of the real-time correlation function of the position operator of the quantum harmonic oscillator at equilibrium within this specific model.  The method utilized to achieve this computation involves slicing the time dimension into discrete segments and employing a Monte Carlo algorithm to evaluate the path integral as a Gaussian multi-dimensional integral.  The paper concludes that the resulting computation yields the same results as the analytical solution for the real-time correlation function in question.

We develop a novel approach to applying Hoare logic in the context of quantum programs, integrating the concept of expectations. By incorporating expectations into our precondition and postcondition specifications, we move beyond traditional quantum invariants, enabling a relational approach that compares the behavior of two programs. This approach allows us to prove the equivalence of two programs, as well as their independence from preconditions and preconditions, streamlining the derivation of common quantum program correctness principles such as invariants and variation bounds. These proof rules form the basis of a relational security model for quantum programs, facilitating the comparison of the behavior of two programs.

The paper addresses the problem of bias in vector magnetic field maps, particularly in estimating the component perpendicular to the line-of-sight, $B_{\perp}$. This issue is addressed by developing an algorithm that incorporates local constraints on magnetic field properties, such as continuity and the absence of electric currents, to refine $B_{\perp}$ estimates. The algorithm's effectiveness is evaluated using synthetic data with known properties and real data from the Hinode satellite's SpectroPolarimeter instrument, which has known biases in initial $B_{\perp}$ estimates. The paper finds that the proposed method can accurately recover both artificial and real magnetic field distributions, even in the presence of noise, and can identify and correct anomalies in $B_{\perp}$ estimates, including those caused by noise and instrument limitations, as well as any biases present in the initial seed estimates, as seen with the Hinode data.

A lattice is considered a boolean lattice if its covering graph forms a bipartite graph. The research has progressed in determining conditions for a lattice to be semi-linear or linear graphs, particularly when the lattice consists of a boolean lattice or a linear graph lattice of an inversion. The objective is to characterize the structure of the lattice of boolean lattices of an inversion, proving that it comprises a direct product of four lattices: the original boolean lattice, the lattice of subsets, and two lattices of special representations.

This research fills the gap in our understanding of the geometry of spacetime by introducing and characterizing timed-like Berendt curves within the framework of semi-metric spaces. To begin with, the paper provides a concise overview of the definition and properties of the geometry of the planet, focusing on the operator $[,\,]$ and its associated properties (1) through (4). This study fills in the detailed outcomes of our investigation into how loss function design influences deep learning models' performance in image classification. We examined the tactics used in training models, including the handling of label encoding, the management of class imbalance through sampling strategies, and the various loss functions that can be utilized. Our comprehensive analysis leveraged a set of increasingly difficult classification problems applied to three widely-used datasets: FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100. We tested on both independently and jointly considered combinations of sampling methods, label encodings, and loss functions. Our findings showcased that models trained with the cross-entropy loss function demonstrated higher accuracy when paired with balanced datasets. We also discovered that addressing class imbalance through uniform or square root encoding, in combination with the cross-entropy loss, yielded the best results. Additionally, we observed that using the weighted exponential loss function could lead to better outcomes in certain scenarios. Our results provide a useful guide for selecting the most effective loss function for specific dataset characteristics.

This study presents a comprehensive dataset consisting of 38,676 logical reasoning tasks, categorized into 541 distinct scenarios, with each scenario further broken down into various aspects. The diverse scenarios reflect real-life situations encountered by individuals, ranging from social gatherings and events to transportation, media consumption, ownership, gifting, and regulatory contexts. Our reasoning framework comprises a combination of formal rules represented in first-order logic and more specific guidelines tailored to each scenario. Researchers can utilize our dataset for training, testing, and analyzing AI models, with options to evaluate them through automated evaluation or manual scrutiny. To facilitate custom analysis, we provide an open platform that allows researchers to define new logical rules and aspects to focus on within a particular scenario. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our dataset and framework, we trained custom models using both neural networks and traditional machine learning techniques, achieving satisfactory results.

Our proposed framework improves predictions for dynamic scenes by integrating two complementary image representations: depth and normal vectors.  The system leverages the predictive capabilities of neural networks while utilizing a recurrence network to generate sequences of images.  Addressing the need for extensive training data, we've developed a strategy to generate more prediction training sets.  Applying this framework to multiple datasets yields significant improvements over existing methods.

A graph's full coordinate system, known as its metrics dimension, may require a large number of points and is susceptible to failure in certain situations. As a result, we are interested in finding a smaller subset of points that still allows us to distinguish between pairs of vertices even after considering their distances to the subset. This variation is called the trimmed metric dimension. We provide a comprehensive overview of the trimmed metric dimension, including its connection to the standard metric dimension, its relation to other derived concepts, and its potential use in graph theory problems such as identifying whether a graph has a unique factorization into connected components. Although some of the existing theorems about metric dimension do not directly apply to the trimmed metric dimension, we identify analogous results for various graph types and operations.

Categorizing heart sounds into normal and abnormal categories is crucial for early disease detection and diagnosis.  While murmuring indicates an abnormality, accurate detection is complicated by ambient noises and the use of inexpensive sensors.  A convolutional neural network is employed in this research to learn the characteristics of heart sounds, focusing on distinguishing normal from abnormal sounds while learning in an environment with noise.  Using a dataset of 5500 signals, researchers developed and tested several noise-infused models, evaluating their performance through k-Nearest Neighbors and decision trees.  Multiple experiments were conducted to assess the effectiveness of the proposed method, with results showing that the model can accurately differentiate between normal and abnormal heart sounds.

We examined the emission lines of neutral ionized carbon (CI) in galaxies, focusing on their luminosity function and characteristic properties. Despite the effectiveness of radio telescopes in detecting line features, especially for smaller galaxies, the observed CI emission appears consistently lower than predicted theoretical models suggest, by a factor of 10 on average. When analyzing the physical parameters of galaxies, including mass and luminosity, as well as star formation rates and gas velocities, a similar discrepancy emerges. Again, the observed values are lower than anticipated, by a factor of 5 on average. When examining the distribution of CI emission luminosity functions across galaxy populations, a similar trend persists. Despite the consistency in spectral line features observed, the application of energy balance principles, considering both stellar radiation and gas turbulence, results in a deficit of energy in heating CI lines, by a factor of 10 on average. This discrepancy may indicate either an unaccounted-upon cooling mechanism, such as a contribution from stellar dust radiation, or a non-Maxwellian energy distribution within the lowest temperature CI line features.

We identify a specific configuration of the ASEP on a one-dimensional lattice with local velocities varying randomly that induces a fundamental relation between times elapsed ASEP models modeled in a multi-player game with three participants. This relationship, which links the ASEP velocity process to a three-player game, is a significant finding. Moreover, we demonstrate that in this particular ASEP model, the velocity process for a tagged particle behaves fundamentally differently from typical ASEP models on lattices with homogeneous conditions, and it converges to a normal distribution as time progresses, in contrast to the usual power-law convergence. This distinct behavior is a noteworthy discovery.

This study examines the use of mathematical models in understanding epidemic outbreaks, with a focus on the ongoing SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. We begin by reviewing basic model types and their limitations, then explore more advanced frameworks that integrate biological data on virus transmission, incorporating individual behaviors, environmental factors, and immunological responses. We discuss the value of these models in predicting outbreaks, predicting the impact of interventions, and predicting the evolution of the virus. Furthermore, we highlight the importance of communicating model predictions effectively to policymakers and the public, emphasizing the need for transparent communication about assumptions, uncertainties, and the potential evolution of the virus.

To address this uncertainty, we developed a modification to the IllustrisTNG simulation that allows us to distinguish between central and satellite galaxies, as well as identify active galactic nucleus (AGN) activity in the model. Using central mass-spectral sequence data from Illustration TNG 2-1 M* 10^9 Solar Masses 10^10, we constructed three simulations that reduce central star formation in massive galaxies, and we compared their outcomes to the modified IllustrisTNG model with distinct central and satellite star formation suppression and only AGN feedback effective in massive satellites. Our results show that to accurately recreate the star formation spectral sequence in Illustration TNG 2-1 M* 10^9 Solar Masses 10^10, we need to suppress star formation in a manner that is independent of a galaxy's location and focus AGN feedback on massive satellite galaxies. This indicates that in our simulation, an external influence, such as tidal torque, is responsible for limiting the availability of gas for star formation in massive galaxies, rather than feedback mechanisms. This paper presents a mult-task learning approach that simultaneously performs cross-domain and cross-language sentiment analysis.

This study presents original observations of the brown dwarf 2M0527-0028, a member of a known triple star system, revealing unexpected spectral characteristics. When integrated with existing data, angular momentum analysis indicates anomalous spinning in the brown dwarf's outer layers, potentially resulting from tidal interactions with a companion M-dwarf, 2M0532-0028, in close proximity. Alternatively, a yet-unconfirmed ultra-cold stellar companion could be responsible for this behavior through a chain of three interacting bodies.

The rapid proliferation of social media has made fake news a pressing concern, with fake videos contributing to the problem in an emerging manner. Although traditional fake news has been effectively tackled, the complexities of fake video dissemination present unique challenges due to its unpredicted characteristics. Our research introduces a comprehensive framework that aims to detect false information with an unprecedented effectiveness, utilizing a two-stage process. The initial phase involves a customizable false news detection model tailored to verified text-modal data, whereas the subsequent phase employs a meta neural process network to detect false videos in an emergent setting without prior video-domain training. A unique false video dataset developed for research purposes, along with existing large-scale information, demonstrates the framework's superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.

This paper presents construction methods for polyphase Golay complementary arrays, which can be used to create Golay complementary sequences when specific conditions are met.
The introduced designs are based on structures already established for Golay complementary pairs and matrices, and they offer a larger capacity compared to previous methods.
In fact, the capacity of the ACAs obtained from our proposed designs is determined by the formula $4m_1m_2N_1N_2$, which is not possible to achieve with the already existing constructions.

In safety-critical sectors like aviation, it is imperative that novel data sources be found that do not harm system performance. Consequently, a constructive approach is required to maintain performance in response to new data sources. This paper presents the key points of our work. Beginning with the algorithm Integrate-NEW, we emphasize its main aspects. Then, we introduce various image manipulation techniques such as cropping, color alteration, and noise alteration, as well as their impact on model performance. Finally, we discuss the concept of cross-model inference and our contribution towards it, highlighting the unified feature extraction approach we've developed using contrastive learning.

Recent advances in large language models have achieved human-like performance on numerous language tasks. However, when it comes to activities involving specialized knowledge, these models often fall short due to their limited knowledge base and frequent hallucinations. To address this, researchers have explored various methods to integrate external knowledge into the model's structure. Yet, existing integration techniques are labor-intensive and do not effectively leverage the organized knowledge available. To resolve this, we propose an automated approach to inferring specialized knowledge into the model's structure, called Structured Knowledge Injection for Large Language Models. By training on high-dimensional vectors from knowledge graphs, these models can accurately answer knowledge-based questions while maintaining efficiency and compatibility with the knowledge graph for further investigation. Our results on three widely used benchmarks demonstrate that our optimized model outperforms other versions of the large language model and directly accesses knowledge graphs.

This study explores how shadow radii of black holes are related to their thermodynamic properties, focusing on non-linear charged AdS black holes, to determine first-order shadow radius and charge radius relationships. Using the Bardeen-Hawking-Payne definition of shadow radius, we calculate the equivalent horizon radius and analyze the phase behavior of black holes, finding a linear connection between shadow radius and horizon radius that mirrors the black hole's non-linear charge and mass relationship. We also investigate how black hole shadow radii are affected by charge and AdS radius, discovering that as charge increases, shadow radius and horizon temperature rise while AdS radius has the opposite effect. Finally, we obtain the shadow radius's relationship with temperature and explore its connection to the bardeen-black hole's phase transition, finding a linear correlation that also reveals a first-order phase transition at critical charge-to-mass ratios.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay mode for the first time and gathered more data on the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^{*0}$ decay, which was previously only partially confirmed. Using 3.0 inverse fermi squared terabbyte samples of $b\bar{d}$ and $s\bar{d}$ pair decays, scientists analyzed data from the LHCa and LHCb detectors. The measured branching fractions were found to be $3.5 (\pm 1.0 (\pm 0.3)) inverse fermi squared terabbyte$ for $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ and $2.7 (\pm 1.1 (\pm 0.5)) inverse fermi squared terabbyte$ for $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$.
This paper introduces an algorithm for constructing the module lattice of submodules from the lattice of submodules of a module's summands, addressing a problem in representation theory.

This paper introduces two new types of hyper surfaces in Euclidean space that possess specific mathematical properties called recurrent and bi-recurrent structures, which are analogous to certain physical phenomena. By leveraging these structures, we identify the following hyper surfaces: uniform hyper planes for surfaces that possess specific properties called harmonic functions; parallel hyper surfaces for ones with similar characteristics; and a combination of a time-like or space-like hyperbola and a real line for ones satisfying additional conditions; all of which are considered hyper surfaces with hyper surfaces that possess characteristics similar to certain wave equations. Additionally, we determine the necessary conditions for these structures to exist on these hyper surfaces, revealing their significance in understanding the behavior of these mathematical objects.

A subportion of the Farey sequence of order 100 displaying the best subportion where a random rational number p/q meets the identifiable condition is displayed to make the definition more understandable. A persistent puzzle in the field of self-organized criticality involves the application of Brownian motion universal functions to the intermittent patterns observed in various natural phenomena. While previous attempts to address this issue have not been successful, especially in the case of adhesive tape peeling experiments where intermittent bursts have been observed, a new model has been developed that explains these patterns without requiring time resampling. This fresh approach takes into account the individual contributions of intermittent bursts to adhesive tape peeling speed in real-time and is supported by the results ofadhesive tape peeling experiments and simulations.

In 1927, Menger developed an interest in the theory of angle spaces, and derived two theorems within this field. The first theorem presented by Menger shows that the theory of angle spaces is equivalent to the theory of metric spaces, but with limitations specific to the Euclidean plane. A prior unresolved issue by Menger concerned the existence of non-Archean angle spaces. A prior unresolved issue by Menger concerned the existence of non-Archean angle spaces. Recently, this prior unresolved issue was resolved by Delaveau and Moulis in 2019, with specific examples of such angle spaces that do not meet the 'every non-zero angle has a complementary counterpart' property. However, it was found that these counter-intuitive angle spaces can only exist in the context of higher-dimensional spaces ($\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \ge 3$). Although it is possible to define an overall metric on such spaces, angle measurement becomes undefined at certain points, similar to how curvature variations affect angle measurement on manifolds. This discovery indicates that to fully capture the structure of such spaces, one must consider higher-order angle definitions, such as the relationship between multiple angles at a specific point, mirining approaches used in differential geometry. On the other hand, Menger's initial theory which focused on measuring angles between disjoint pairs of points is insufficient for describing the architecture of such spaces.

Point Cloud Models used in 3D visualization often suffer from coarse resolutions and missing details, prompting a need for high-quality post-processing. Existing smoothers use convolutional neural networks face efficiency issues due to large model sizes and slow processing speeds. Our proposed method, Transformation-Unique Smoothing (TPC), leverages a prior ODE solver for better performance by using input point order as a unique initial condition, eliminating the need for a shared network. On standard benchmark datasets, TPC outperforms current methods with significant gains in FS and mFS scores (43.49 and 35.63 respectively), reduces model size by over 100 times, and enhances processing speeds by over 10 times, while also showing strong generalizability across various point cloud architectures.

The integration of formal verification and testing in programming has given rise to the concept of extending testing with geometry, which guarantees that a test is representative of a program's overall structure. This guarantee is achieved by guaranteeing that the test geometrically centroid the program's code graph, dispelling the possibility of hidden errors, and enabling the amplification of testing effectiveness through the strategic selection of test inputs, such as exploiting the sensitivity of certain tests to specific vulnerabilities, all for free in terms of computational resources and test execution time. We have used Levenshtein distances to evaluate the centrality and centroid of tests, and applied program transformation techniques to identify tests that satisfy these requirements, revealing the potential benefits of this approach and its practical implications through existing research and case studies.

Advanced composite materials that incorporate nanofillers into polymer matrices have a potential application in engineering structures subject to constant loads and undergoing deformations, where their conductive properties can be used to monitor their own integrity.  
To fully utilize this conductive behavior for structural health monitoring purposes, it is crucial that the relationship between mechanical damage and changes in electrical conductivity remains accurate.  
Although previous research has attempted to model this relationship, often using equivalent circuit models that divide the material into regions with varying conductivities, these approaches may lack precision when it comes to accurately predicting conductivity changes.  
In contrast, genetic algorithms can be used to create a truly three-dimensional image of a material's electrical properties, providing a more precise mapping of the relationship between mechanical damage and variations in electrical conductivity.  
This technique is particularly relevant in the design of self-sensing composites, ensuring that their conductive behavior can be used effectively to monitor their own integrity.

This work redefines the tensor formalism of a Euclidean space by employing only geometric concepts such as angles, lengths, and vector operations, reserving vector products for perpendicular vectors. Consequently, the tensor rank reduction techniques and associated theorems can be proven using basic geometric principles, eliminating the need for vector product definitions for arbitrary vectors.

This work presents an improved fast approximation of a matrix's inverse, building upon the HMOR method and reducing its error order from 3 to 5.

The application of contextual linear bandits has seen a significant upsurge with the emergence of resource-constrained devices in the context of large-scale systems. A key challenge that arises involves quickly adapting to contextual linear bandit problems with a substantial action space on these devices in a fully decentralized environment where contextual information varies across devices at each time step. A sophisticated algorithm has been developed specifically for this scenario, leveraging an efficient local learning strategy that reduces the contextual linear bandit violation while promoting the exchange of parameter estimates among neighboring devices. The theoretical guarantees provided demonstrate that the described algorithm achieves a bound of $O(d\sqrt{T} + \sqrt{N}t_0+\frac{p_0}\tau_0})$ for the violation of regret, with a communication complexity of $O(\log(\frac{\Delta_{TCB}}{\delta}))$ to achieve the same outcome with a confidence level of $1-\delta$.

A phenomenon called vertical shear instability (VSI) is observed in protoplanetary disks and is influenced by dust evolution processes. 
The VSI generates turbulence that should theoretically accelerate the clustering of particles, yet its contribution is often negated by other forces like gravity and magnetic fields in the disk's outer areas. To investigate how dust evolution influences VSI, we created three different models representing disks with varying levels of particle growth, and we analyzed their thermal structures and energy distribution. Our findings indicate that as particles accumulate and form clumps, the effectiveness of the VSI in producing turbulence decreases due to changes in velocity profiles and temperature gradients within the disks. We calculated the accretion rates caused by VSI-induced turbulence in the outer regions of the disks and found that as particles mature and clumping occurs, these rates decline significantly. The VSI may be responsible for generating millimeter-sized particles and causing a peak in emission around 1 cm, but it's unlikely to explain the disk-mass distribution observed in brown dwarf formation. The results highlight the connection between dust evolution and disk turbulence, suggesting a more complex relationship as particles mature and form rocks, metals, and planetesimals. The findings emphasize the importance of considering a model that simultaneously accounts for dust evolution and disk turbulence when studying planet formation.

This research focuses on harmonic functions within the context of a particular type of manifold where the Ricci curvature decreases over time and the manifold's scalar curvature remains constant. A key theorem established by Li and Yau on convex functions in a specific type of manifold is extended to prove that only trivial functions satisfy a given condition.

Recent advancements in outsourcing training and machine learning as a service have created innovative threats such as hidden functionalities that are embedded in artificial neural networks. What sets the research described in this paper apart is its focus on a novel network architecture that is adapted for threat detection purposes. This research aims to find efficient and effective ways to implant malicious capabilities in neural networks that are used for processing images, contrasting with previous efforts that were complicated to implement or had poor success rates. The new method identifies an essential area in the convolutional neural network layers where the backdoor functionality will be trained, discovering an optimal pattern that triggers the harmful behavior. Statistical analysis reveals that the research achieved impressive results with 100% success rates in implanting various functionalities into popular neural network models such as ResNet18 and ResNet50, contrasting with previous findings.

In the context of a distributed machine learning system where data varies across local environments, a graceful method is required to update models given computational and communication constraints. A local model update is necessary for accurate learning, yet it can lead to bias when fast clients are prioritized. To effectively learn from heterogeneous data environments, a fair client selection strategy is essential. Our proposed federated learning framework integrates these requirements, ensuring fair access for all environments while efficiently updating models. By leveraging a random walk technique, we guarantee that every environment is updated over time, reducing communication needs by skipping unnecessary participation. We evaluate our framework on image and sound recognition tasks using various datasets, demonstrating its superior performance in handling heterogeneous data environments compared to existing methods.

ward space, all applicable operations are already implemented, eliminating the need for additional implementations such as KL diver-
gence, and making the method particularly suitable for quick deployment. To further enhance performance, we also propose an active
learning strategy. Evaluations on four publicly available datasets and several medically relevant synthetic datasets demonstrate that
our proposed technique outperforms existing methods.

In the framework of quantum mechanics, the concept of steering originates from the work of Schr\"odinger and represents a phenomenon where a player's state can be manipulated by another player's measurements. Although some perspectives consider it indeterminate or even equivalent to quantified fairness between players, we demonstrate its actual significance by establishing its connection to single-particle entanglement. As a result, we confirm that steering possesses true nonlocal characteristics, distinct from the typical definition, and confirm its validity through an experiment that violates its corresponding inequality, which is derived from the single-particle fairness assumption.

The integration of Artificial Intelligence techniques and improved information systems within the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) sector presents significant potential, yet it also presents substantial challenges related to data privacy, security concerns, and data silos. Federated Learning has been shown to effectively mitigate these issues, but further improvement is possible through the utilization of Blockchain technology. To facilitate the efficient utilization of Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning in IoV systems, we have conducted an in-depth review of related research and identified several key directions for future work, which include developing dynamic data partitioning and optimization frameworks, creating robust security protocols to guard against malicious activities, designing intelligent missing value imputation methods, exploring the potential of Blockchain for value exchange and data ownership management within FL systems, and developing centralized management frameworks for large-scale implementations.

This work presents an end-to-end neural network architecture designed for video identification that prioritizes real-time processing on resource-constrained devices.  
The core of this multi-classification system, which comprises 1000 classes across 32 frames per video, is an LSTM-based model. Given the complex nature of LSTM networks, we propose a 5-bit quantization scheme that linearly approximates the underlying function without incurring an exponential growth in error. The resulting system, named LiteDeep, achieves accurate video identification outcomes, outperforming previous approaches that expand LSTM networks, and meets specified performance targets.

This paper investigates solutions to the Schrödinger equation that exhibit explosive behavior when initialized outside a convex obstacle under the focus-trapping condition. By employing a novel approach, we identify the first instances of such explosive solutions within a mass-suppressed regime near the explosion threshold. Conversely, we also establish that solutions are bounded under a slightly more restrictive mass-regime. The determined explosion threshold is influenced by both the initial mass and the curvature of the obstacle's boundary. These findings indicate that both the geometry of the obstacle and the initial data contribute to the phenomenon of explosive solutions, which theoretically could correspond to particle generation effects like the Schwinger effect or Unruh effect.

We provide a novel proof of a conjecture by Cheater and a theorem by Abbes, showing that local varieties within a given variety behave nicely under modification in a neighborhood of a given point in a positive-characteristic setting.

Hypothesis testing methods in statistics have long been debated, with Bayes factors recently gaining popularity due to a perceived shift away from traditional testing practices. This trend is exacerbated by an increasing reliance on automated hypothesis testing, such as in machine learning workflows. Despite its importance, there is a lack of consensus on the best practices for using Bayes factors effectively. We propose a comprehensive guide outlining key considerations for analyzing and reporting Bayes factor results, drawing on mathematical principles, established Bayesian inference practices, and feasible computational approaches. This decision framework is illustrated with real-world data from sports research, demonstrating the implementation of these recommendations.

Discourse indicators such as you know, sort of, and actually bridge gaps between conversational segments but their usage is context dependent leading to misunderstandings. To improve machine readability of conversations our goal is to train a model specifically for discourse indicators using 31 different types. Our annotated dataset named DiscSense comprises 115000 unique discourse indicators with contextual meanings identified in English conversations. Each indicator is categorized into 17 broad groups including agreement, contrast, and clarification. To verify the effectiveness of DiscSense our we developed a discourse prediction model that outperforms existing frameworks trained on smaller datasets. Furthermore we created 113 contextual examples showcasing the utility of DiscSense for research on discourse indicators.
This study establishes the one-parameter family of deformations of the Jordanian twist within the rational Jordan algebra associated with the $sl_2$ Lie algebra.

This researchAddresses the creation of an algorithm for automatically verifying the satisfaction of regular expression patterns incorporated in software configurations and access control mechanisms. We have developed an algorithm that can analyze a specific type of equivalence relation between extended regular expressions, which include features like character classes, complements, and intersections. As the set of infinite strings that match these types of regular expressions form a specific subclass of automata with finite states, we can convert the expression under investigation into an equivalent form, potentially optimizing the resulting automaton with finite states. The critical challenge we are addressing involves determining if a specific feature is embedded within a different, potentially more restricted, regular expression pattern; the approach we have developed is a symbolic method for resolving this type of comparison. We have tested our algorithm by applying it to real-world scenarios and found that the resulting regular expression constraints integrated into software configurations can pose a complex problem of nested inference, which the symbolic solver can effectively address. As a result, we have established the usefulness of the tool for analyzing regular expression patterns in software configurations and verified its effectiveness through experiments.

Building upon previous work by \cite{Ferrara:1971vh}, \cite{Ferrara:1973vz}, we develop a comprehensive integral representation of the conformal block in CFT$_2$ suitable for its application in an AdS$_2$ context. This integral representation is utilized to derive a closed-form expression for the highest weight operator that generates spinless descendants in a CFT$_2$ context. Additionally, we obtain a closed-form expression for the spinning conformal block when conformal primary operators are in the vacuum state on the boundary of AdS$_2$. This result enables us to determine the precise closed-form expression for the spinning highest weight operator and its application in generating spinning descendants within a CFT$_2$ context.

To wide-field X-ray monitors based on lobster-eye microsphere optics, a novel configuration is presented that employs a multiplexed detection system. In this setup, several focal planes are positioned at varying distances behind the optic's surface, allowing a single array of X-ray detectors to fulfill the focal plane array's role. This innovative design enables the creation of large-scale, cost-effective wide-field X-ray monitors with enhanced angular resolution by leveraging the natural variation in sphere curvature towards the optic's periphery. The feasibility of this concept is verified through simulations using the XMM-Newton detector response, demonstrating that sphere-induced focusing effects allow for distinct image formation on separate focal planes. The optimal arrangement of these focal planes can be determined through optimization algorithms, and the resulting configuration's performance is evaluated both with simulated data and actual observations of active galactic nuclei and pulsars, showing that this design effectively preserves image resolution and source detectability.

This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the impact of dark matter halo properties on the performance of large-scale structure surveys, utilizing a sophisticated deep learning model, HiLDA. The underlying theoretical framework employs a stochastic field theory, with a focus on a novel cosmic speed potential. Through simulations generated by the $N$-body cosmological code MovingMesh, the research identifies the most informative halo characteristics for survey efficiency, with halo mass being the most prominent factor, albeit in a non-linear manner. The research also reveals that halo velocity, in particular the cosmic speed potential, exhibits a non-linear correlation with halo density. The resulting probability density functions illustrate the potential of the cosmic speed potential in predicting halo velocity, making it a promising observable for future surveys designed to detect large-scale structures.

This research explores the application of atomic interferometry for extremely precise measurements of local magnetic field changes, leveraging a phenomenon where superconducting materials expel magnetic fields, referred to as the Meissner effect. By employing a two-point differential method, our setup is capable of canceling out the influence of vibrations and tidal effects on the detection process. A unique experimental configuration that employs a ring-shaped region of trapped magnetic field has been designed and implemented, showcasing an improvement in measurement sensitivity by a factor of 100, achieving a sensitivity of 50 fT/square root Hz at a frequency of 0.1 Hz. Moreover, the system's capability to detect local magnetic field changes is demonstrated by observing a small current-induced variation.

A comprehensive theoretical framework has been developed to predict the spectral characteristics of magnetic impurities located on the surface of a superconducting material. This material-specific model focuses on a manganese adatom and small clusters on the Nb(110) surface and incorporates an accurate description of the superconducting gap and a precise approach to determine the magnetic moment. By applying this framework, the spectral characteristics of various cluster configurations can be simulated and the optimal arrangement on the superconducting surface can be identified. Additionally, the model can predict the occurrence of non-trivial bound states, such as the even-odd effect and higher-order Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states, on the density of states of the superconducting surface. These characteristics allow for the differentiation of cluster configurations with identical magnetic moments but different configurations.

This report details our methods that led to 3rd and 4th place rankings in tasks 1 and 2 at the 2019 CEC competition, focusing on skin cancer diagnosis using a dataset of 5000 clinical images. We employed a variant of the ResNet50 architecture, pre-trained on ImageNet, and used the K-means algorithm to identify and discard outlier data to improve model accuracy. Our best results were achieved without resampling the dataset, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach in achieving high accuracy rates of 97.2%, 99.2%, and 98.7% for correct, misdiagnosed, and uncertain image classifications, respectively, in the test set of 500 images.

The simplicity of forward Compton scattering allows for the application of the Weaverbition approximation, similar to the Wayberbition process, to improve computational efficiency. This article examines the conditions under which invariant sets form in dynamical systems, focusing on invariant surfaces in three-dimensional systems. While previous research has identified conditions that lead to these surfaces, we explore and discuss the specific requirements and their implications, especially in fractional-order dynamical systems.

This study presents experimental results demonstrating the feasibility of obtaining source images from measured receptor data, bypassing the need for initial source information, using the ADAM iterative algorithm. Two experiments were conducted with source-receiver setups that produced receptor signals, which served as input for source image reconstruction. Notably, source characteristics such as location and frequency remain unknown at the onset of the iterative process. It was found that source estimation is feasible despite acoustic interference patterns created by the speaker and microphone system, as well as room acoustic effects, which cause convergence issues. In both experiments, source images with high accuracy were produced within a reasonable number of iterations, validating the effectiveness of adaptive iterative techniques for source reconstruction in complex acoustic environments, even when initial source information is unavailable.

Within the simplest variation of the scoto-seesaw model, we investigate the mechanism behind the neutronoless double beta decay process. By optimizing the parameters of the effective Majorana neutrino mass, we determine lower limits on the neutrinoless double beta decay mass scale. This, in turn, imposes constraints on the mass of the lightest heavy neutrino and the coupling strength between it and the vacuum expectation value of a neutral scalar field. Additionally, we explore the potential for a type-II seesaw mechanism to occur and investigate its implications. As a result, we predict the existence of additional heavy neutrinos and may even observe it through future experiments. Furthermore, we integrate existing constraints and theoretical limits on vacuum stability and the generation of electroweak symmetry breaking. This leads us to determine the minimum possible mass for the lightest dark matter particle and the coupling strength between it and the median heavy neutrino. Finally, we present a feasible parameter set for a fully functional model as a proof of concept.
